answer: Identity verification requires each proposed identity to advance its own modular-squaring chain, xᵢ₊₁ = xᵢ² mod N, through a prescribed number of sequential steps before its Wesolowski proof can be checked. GPUs can run separate chains concurrently, but cannot remove the dependency between steps in one chain; creating many clones therefore requires additional parallel hardware and elapsed time, imposing a physical rate limit across onyx, mesa, and atlas.
